dialogue.user: Hi there! I'm looking for a new book. I'm interested in science fiction, and I'm hoping to find something in the $30 to $60 price range with at least a 2.0 rating. What do you have that fits that description?
dialogue.agent:
Here are a few science fiction books that fit your criteria:

*   **Gentle Giants of Ganymede**: This book has an average rating of 4.8/5 and 5 reviews. It is priced at $82.42.
*   ***More science fiction tales;: Crystal creatures, bird-things, & other weirdies***: This book has an average rating of 4.7/5 with 1 review and costs $49.99.
*   **Glassford Girl: Complete Series (Parts 1 through 4) (Emily Heart Time Jumper Series)**: This book has an average rating of 4.6/5 with 1 review and is priced at $30.24.
*   *"The Best of John W. Campbell"*: This book has an average rating of 4.5/5 with 5 reviews and is priced at $50.95.

Glassford Girl: Complete Series (Parts 1 through 4) (Emily Heart Time Jumper Series)
products.description: From the Author When I began this series, I initially wanted to create a lovable teenage homeless girl who was struggling to survive life on the streets. What I ended up with was something completely different. Emily Heart came alive on the pages and touched my heart, leading me down a path of self-discovery right along with her. She's not just a 15-year-old girl who's burdened with an uncontrollable time jumping condition. She's a deeply caring, powerfully strong young lady with an unwavering will to survive. She has rules that she lives by, but finds that sometimes rules must be broken, even if it means that she might become too emotional and simply blink out of existence. Finding love is dangerous for everyone, but for Emily Heart it can mean the end of all that she is.Life on this planet isn't fun or fair for most of us, but for Emily Heart, life is all she wants. Fair or unfair, just making it through another day is reward enough. About the Author Jay J. Falconer is a award-winning, Amazon #1 Bestselling Author in Action & Adventure, Military Sci-Fi, Post-Apocalyptic, Young Adult, and Men's Adventure fiction. He lives in the high mountains of northern Arizona where the brisk, clean air and stunning views inspire his day. When he's not busy working on his next novel, he's out training, shooting, hunting, or preparing for whatever comes next.You can find more information about this Top-5 Science Fiction author and his books at JayFalconer.com, or on twitter at: @JayJFalconer, or on Facebook at: facebook.com/NarrowsOfTime/2016 Gold Medalist: Best Dystopia Book, Readers' Favorite International Book Awards2017 Gold Medalist: Best Young Adult Action Book, Readers' Favorite International Book AwardsAmazon Kindle Scout Winning Author

dialogue.user: That's a good start, but Gentle Giants of Ganymede is a bit outside my budget. The other three look promising though. Can you tell me a little more about ***More science fiction tales;: Crystal creatures, bird-things, & other weirdies*** and "The Best of John W. Campbell"? I'm particularly interested in what they're about.
dialogue.agent:
***More science fiction tales;: Crystal creatures, bird-things, & other weirdies*** is priced at $49.99 and has an average rating of 4.7/5 with 1 review. The description is not available.

"**The Best of John W. Campbell**" is priced at $50.95 and has an average rating of 4.5/5 with 5 reviews. This book features classic science fiction stories such as "Who Goes There?" (which the movie The Thing was based on), "Twilight," and "The Machine." It also includes "The Visions of John W. Campbell," which seems to be an introduction to the collection.

CAMPBELL Here are the finest stories by the man who almost single-handedly created modern science fiction--the writer who taught a generation to dream...and to write of all possible futures. TWILIGHT He was a mere hitchhiker now, but he had once seen the far, far future...and had returned to mourn what he had seen! THE MACHINE The machine was ultimately benevolent...so benevolent that it gave mankind the ultimate but most unwanted gift! FORGETFULNESS They were like children in the museum of Earth's glorious past...children who had forgotten so much, but whose powers were those of gods! And the classic that was to become the movie THE THING: WHO GOES THERE? The Thing was the most dreadful threat men had ever faced...a creature that could be any one--or all--of them! And many more! top_reviews.title: A nice bit of nostalgia
top_reviews.text:
I read this book over thirty years ago, back in elementary school, and I remember how much I enjoyed it then.
Yes, this is geared more toward younger readers, but I still really liked reading it again at my middle age.

"The Music of Minox" was an interesting adventure, and I still remember the shock I had as a young boy reading about how the monsters in this story had so horribly maimed one of the characters in it.
I suppose you could say a youngster would be a bit startled by that.

"The Hole in Jennifer's Room" was interesting, and the very ending is rather jarring.
Just a hint of Rod Serling in this one.

"Werewolf Girl" was amusing, especially for anyone who ever wondered what it would be like to change completely.

"A Thirst for Blood" was a take on what would happen if a young man became a fugitive from his own ancient people.
This one was a bit alarming, given the subject matter, but the ending neatly wraps it up.

"Hide and Seek" was definitely one of the stronger stories, with an ending that reminds the reader of the virtue of sacrifice and gratitude.

"The Thing From Ennis Rock" was one that immediately interested me, having been a major dinosaur buff as far back as I can remember.
It was a really good story that spends most of the time being another adventure, then it has an ending that has echoes of Steinbeck, which really surprised me.
No, the writing is certainly not in the same league as that of Steinbeck, but the melancholy is there.
Really good story here.

Which leads me to what I consider the best story found in this book, "The Bend of Time."
This one story truly is haunting, and it so well explains how important one person can be for the future, good or bad.
Reading this story, three decades after I first did, I was swept back to that time, sitting in Wilbur Wright Elementary library.
This one story was the one that told me that I would be reading scores of more science fiction books in the future.
Superb story.

Anyone wanting this book for kids should be aware that, while there is nothing overly gruesome or scary for most, some of the very young or more sensitive kids might not be quite ready for it, as each story has elements that could inspire nightmares.
However, were this a movie instead of a story, I would rate it as PG, with some elements that might be PG-13.
It's a nice compilation.
